video_directives: Inject a faster mid-video beat spike — the 1883 and gauge cards sit 3-4 seconds each with only subtle background motion; a quicker cut or mini-reveal would lift tempo.
Give the volcano/hook composition a small continuous idle animation (crown pulse, ember drift is there but faint) so the opening 3-second hold never feels frozen.
Tighten the ear-diagram beat (10-13s) — the '130 dB = PAIN' card holds a touch long with only one shockwave repetition; two pulses suffice before the CRACK cut.

top3_directives: Add subtle warm rim-light on the volcano's dark face (currently near-flat brown) to sell the eruption glow as the light source
Bottom text band reads slightly pasted-on — add a soft gradient feather or widen the band edge so the horizontal seam blends into the sky
Moon and orbit arcs are nearly invisible at phone brightness; nudge their luminance ~15% so they reward the eye path instead of dying in the corner
Move the character off the lower-left corner clutter zone — it partially collides with the 'JAVA' label and its glow bleeds into the shoreline, muddying the clean volcano focal axis
Add a subtle rim-light or warm reflection on the water from the volcano's crater glow to unify the purple sky and blue sea halves, which currently feel like two unrelated color worlds
Raise the water ripple lines' contrast slightly — they vanish on a 6-inch daylight screen, leaving the bottom third reading as a flat dead zone
'AGAIN.' is dark gray on dark navy — nearly invisible on a daylight phone screen. Brighten it to match the cream headline or add an outline/glow.
Character and text overlap awkwardly: the figure's arm cuts into 'IT COULD'. Add clearance or move the figure fully left of the text block.
Waterline horizon sits behind the headline, causing faint horizontal line clashes through the letters — either deepen the water band contrast or raise the text above it.
Fix 'PRESSURE WAVE' legibility: dark gray thin type on dark navy ground will die in daylight — bump to cream/off-white with subtle glow or letter-spacing-preserving weight increase
Fill the dead top third (starfield does nothing) by scaling the gauge up ~15% and pulling the needle glow/arc closer to the danger zone for tension

Resolve the bottom-left character zone: the dim stick figure competes with the gauge as a second focal point while sitting in murk — either light it with the same wave-rim glow as the rings or crop it tighter for punch
Boost the lower-third scene's exposure/key light — the hoodie character and ocean are nearly invisible on a 6-inch daylight screen
Fill the dim mid-band between the ear and caption with a subtle glow or motion element to close the dead zone
Enlarge the '130 dB = PAIN' caption ~30% with a soft dark plate or stroke so it pops off the purple gradient
Enlarge the 'EARDRUMS SPLIT' caption — monospace line at that size risks legibility on a 6-inch phone in daylight; bolden or add a soft dark plate behind it

The glowing character bottom-left competes with the ship/ray focal cluster and floats over dark empty water — either move him into the composition's eye path or anchor him with stronger ground shadow/scale
The rays' salmon color clashes slightly with the violet palette — tint rays toward the palette (warm violet/magenta) and add a subtle glow so the sound feels integrated, not pasted
Fill the upper 45% dead zone — the empty purple sky is a huge dead area; push the BOOM/sunrise motif higher or enlarge the character so vertical space is used
Unify the two text systems — the big BOOM display text and the separate subtitle pill read as competing caption styles; merge into one caption system or restyle the pill to match

Relocate the character — it's crammed into the bottom-left corner with its head clipped by the caption pill; center-right placement with breathing room would give a cleaner eye path from text to subject
Lift the bottom third out of the murk: the right half of the lower band is a large near-black dead zone — add subtle ground texture or rim light to balance the composition
Increase the mascot's presence: its dim underlighting and small size compete weakly with the planet; a warmer key light or slightly larger scale would create a proper two-subject eye path
The orbit ring's teal satellite gets visually swallowed crossing the planet's limb — add a slight glow halo or outline separation so the orbital element reads at 6 inches
Fill the large dead zone in the lower two-thirds — the sea is a near-black void; add subtle wave texture, moon reflection, or ambient detail so the character doesn't float in emptiness

Establish a single focal point: the character is tiny (bottom-right) while the text sits mid-frame with nothing connecting them — enlarge/reposition the character or add a sightline/light cue linking text to subject

Raise foreground/background separation: the subtitle 'THE SEA TOOK THEM' sits dangerously close to the horizon line and the moon is nearly swallowed by the sky — add glow rim or darken backdrop behind text for daylight-phone legibility
Resolve the dual focal point: the character and the volcano compete at similar visual weight — dim/shrink the character or reposition it so the volcano-summit reads first
Fill the dead upper third: empty starfield with no content for ~30% of frame height — add layered cloud wisps or a subtle vignette push toward the summit
Tie the orange circle motif to the message: the large ring passes awkwardly through both subjects with no purpose — either frame the summit glow tightly with it or remove it
The quote line 'CHILD OF KRAKATOA' is dark text over the dark volcano silhouette — add a subtle dark scrim/backing plate or brighten it so it survives daylight phone viewing
Bottom-right quadrant is a large dead zone: either shift the presenter character toward center-right, or extend the ocean highlight/ripple detail to balance the frame
The label chip sits flush over the volcano apex, visually colliding with the smoke puffs above — nudge it down 60-80px or shrink it so the glow summit reads cleanly
Character sits in lower-left with glow; add a subtle rim-light step or vignette to unify him with the mountain's light source
Bottom third is a large near-dead zone of flat navy — add water reflections of the eruption glow to extend the focal path
Mountain silhouette edges are slightly soft/muddy against purple glow — tighten the rim highlight for a crisper focal subject
